title: To take certain Federal lands located in El Dorado County, California, into trust for the benefit of the Shingle Springs Band of Miwok Indians, and for other purposes.
official_summary:
(This measure has not been amended since it was reported to the House on September 10, 2013. The summary of that version is repeated here.)

Takes specified federal land in El Dorado County, California, into trust for the Shingle Springs Band of Miwok Indians.

Describes that land as the approximately 40.852 acres of federal land under the administrative jurisdiction of the Bureau of Land Management (BLM) identified as "Conveyance boundary" on the map titled "Shingle Springs Land Conveyance/Draft" and dated June 7, 2012, including improvements and appurtenances thereto.

Prohibits class II and III gaming on such lands.

summary.headline: This law moves about 40 acres of federal land in El Dorado County, California, into trust for the Shingle Springs Band of Miwok Indians.
summary.what_it_does: The law takes specified federal land managed by the Bureau of Land Management and places it into trust for the Shingle Springs Band of Miwok Indians. The land covers roughly 40.852 acres, as shown on a map dated June 7, 2012, and includes its improvements and related rights. The law also bars class II and class III gaming, which are types of tribal gambling, on that land.

who_it_affects.group: The Shingle Springs Band of Miwok Indians
who_it_affects.how: The tribe gains trust status over about 40 acres of land that was previously federal land managed by the Bureau of Land Management.

who_it_affects.group: Residents and landowners near the parcel in El Dorado County
who_it_affects.how: The land moves out of federal management and into tribal trust, which changes which government holds and manages it.

who_it_affects.group: Visitors and businesses seeking tribal gaming in the area
who_it_affects.how: Class II and class III gaming are not allowed on the transferred land.
